transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Anita Patel (Helix Head of InfoSec), Oliver Grant (Cloud Architect), Samir Bose (Procurement)
Recording id: helix-20250821-16z

Summary: quick SIG/CAIQ walkthrough and evidence mapping, confirm SOC 2 and KMS/HSM approach, data residency questions for EU/UK, next steps to exchange artifacts and schedule HSM deep dive. Transcript quality: medium (some automated transcript errors expected)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for making time today, this is Maya from Redwood Inference. Carlos from our infra team is with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Anita Patel: Hi Maya, good thanks. We have Oliver and Samir on, we'll go through the vendor questionnaire, we sent over the baseline SIG earlier.
[00:20] Carlos Rivera: Great, thanks Anita. Quick note on names—my audio might get a little echo but I'll share my screen with the CAIQ crosswalk in a moment.
[00:30] Oliver Grant: Thanks, and small ask: we are especially interested on the encryption side, KMS, HSM stuff, and also the retention/audit log controls.
[00:40] Samir Bose: From procurement we're mostly timing and any contractual assurances, plus SSO/SCIM and SAML stuff for provisioning.
[00:50] Maya Chen: Perfect. Agenda: 1) SOC2/ISO evidence and CAIQ/SIG mapping 2) RBAC/SSO and provisioning 3) Encryption key management and HSM details 4) Data residency and logs 5) open Q&A and next steps. Anything to add?
[01:12] Anita Patel: No that covers it. We'll probably dig into logging retention and audit capability.
[02:05] Carlos Rivera: (screen shared) Ok I'm bringing up the CAIQ matrix—note our auto-tool produced a preliminary mapping already, but there are a couple of shorthand items where the speech-to-text sometimes garbled acronyms, so please excuse if you see C A I Q spelled out a few ways.
[02:30] Oliver Grant: haha yeah that's fine. On the CAIQ, in the data flow we noticed references to cache - is that KV cache correct? The doc says "K V cash" in a few places so we wanted to confirm.
[02:45] Carlos Rivera: Yes that's KV cache, it's our inference runtime cache for prefix tokens, not a persistent store. We do not persist customer prompt content in the cache beyond short-term session usage, and we can configure TTLs.
[03:10] Maya Chen: Quick clarification: SOC two is available—SOC 2 Type II—that's what we'll share. We also have a set of penetration test summaries and an ISO 27001 certificate for our control plane.
[03:30] Anita Patel: Excellent. We'll need the SOC 2 PDF and the mapping to SIG controls. Can you also call out where audit logs are kept and retention windows?
[03:45] Carlos Rivera: Audit logs are written to our central logging cluster; for hosted customers logs are retained 90 days by default in the console and longer via add-on retention. For Dedicated/Private deployments, retention is customer-configurable and can be shipped to customer-managed logging endpoints (S3, Splunk, etc.).
[04:12] Oliver Grant: Is that encrypted at rest? Where are the keys?
[04:25] Carlos Rivera: Yes, logs at rest are encrypted using our cloud K M S, with envelope encryption and customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) supported in Private deployments. For Hosted we use Redwood-managed KMS by default but you can opt into a CMEK flow.
[04:58] Anita Patel: We require H S M backed keys for some workloads. Do you support HSM or FIPS-validated hardware?
[05:10] Carlos Rivera: We do support H S M-backed key storage when customers use Dedicated or Private with a KMS integration. For Hosted, we can provide HSM-backed CMEK via cloud provider integrations—but we should map the exact provider and proof; I'll add that to action items.
[05:35] Samir Bose: Procurement note: does Redwood have attestations for key management—like KMS supplier certs or how do we get evidence for H S M?
[05:45] Maya Chen: We'll include links to the KMS integration docs and any vendor attestations we can share under NDA. Also, we'll send a CAIQ crosswalk that highlights where evidence exists and where we need to provide artifacts.
[06:20] Oliver Grant: On RBAC: do you integrate with our SAML S S O and SCIM for user provisioning? Also roles for least privilege?
[06:35] Carlos Rivera: Yes we support S A M L 2.0 SSO, SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle, and fine-grained RBAC in the Console. Roles are customizable and we have audit trails for admin actions. One caveat: in Hosted plans some advanced RBAC features are for enterprise tiers only.
[06:58] Anita Patel: Can you demonstrate an audit trail entry? We need to confirm immutable logs for admin activity.
[07:10] Carlos Rivera: I can show a sample from our staging logs—note this is sanitized and the transcript might omit exact timestamps. (shares sample) You can see admin.user.update with actor, time, and request payload hashed. The audit stream can be exported to a customer SIEM.
[08:00] Oliver Grant: Good. Regarding data residency—Helix needs EU mainland residency for certain PII workloads. Do you have EU zones, and can we force processing region?
[08:15] Maya Chen: We operate regional deployments and can pin model serving to EU regions for Private and Dedicated; Hosted customers can choose EU-hosted tenancy. For strict residency we recommend Private deployments with a VPC and regional control plane.
[08:45] Anita Patel: For Hosted, is there a contractual data residency guarantee or just operational practice?
[08:55] Maya Chen: We have contractual addenda for data processing and residency for enterprise agreements. We'll attach the DPA language and region controls.
[09:20] Samir Bose: On the SIG questionnaire you marked some questions as "shared"—can you elaborate?
[09:36] Carlos Rivera: Sure. Example: network perimeter hardening—Redwood manages the service layer and hypervisor for Hosted. Customers are responsible for their application-layer encryption and tenant configuration. We'll show the exact switching in the CAIQ cell where we indicated "shared" and provide justification text.
[10:05] Oliver Grant: There's also a question about model provenance and training data. We need to know what models are used and if any customer data could be used for training.
[10:24] Maya Chen: Redwood does not use customer data from Hosted inference to retrain public models. We can offer options for isolation. We'll provide the policy doc on data usage; there are also options for opt-out and private model pinning in Dedicated/Private.
[10:50] Anita Patel: Good. We'll need that policy and an attestation.
[11:10] Carlos Rivera: Noted. On encryption in transit—TLS 1.2/1.3 is used everywhere, mutual-TLS is available for private peering.
[11:28] Oliver Grant: And for keys, do you support rotation policies and key versioning?
[11:36] Carlos Rivera: Yes. KMS keys have rotation and versioning; for CMEK you'll manage rotation or we can automate rotation with customer approval.
[12:05] Samir Bose: For procurement, can you summarize the fastest route to a pilot with the least friction?
[12:15] Maya Chen: For evaluation, hosted API with restricted dataset is fastest—no infra changes. If Helix requires EU residency and HSM-backed keys, then a Dedicated pilot is common. We can do a 30-day pilot on Dedicated capacity with limited commit.
[12:40] Anita Patel: We prefer Dedicated for pilot if it gives us more control.
[12:48] Maya Chen: Great. We'll note that.
[13:05] Carlos Rivera: Back to the CAIQ rows—there are items asking for MFA enforcement for admins. We enforce MFA for Redwood console and support SSO-enforced MFA via IdP.
[13:30] Oliver Grant: Are there privileged access reviews and just-in-time admin escalation?
[13:45] Carlos Rivera: We have role reviews and SSO provisioning can be tied into your identity governance. JIT admin just-in-time is supported via integrations, but for Hosted it's part of the enterprise feature set.
[14:10] Anita Patel: On penetration testing—do you allow Helix to run its own tests or do you only accept vendor pen test reports?
[14:25] Maya Chen: For Hosted we typically provide our third-party pentest reports. For Dedicated/Private, we can coordinate controlled tests under a test-window and NDA. We'll need to schedule and agree on target IPs.
[14:55] Samir Bose: How about encryption of backups and manifests?
[15:05] Carlos Rivera: Backups are encrypted in transit and at rest with envelope encryption; for Private deployments, backup destinations can be customer-controlled and encrypted with customer keys.
[15:35] Oliver Grant: There's a SIG question about vulnerability management and patching cadence. What's your lifecycle?
[15:45] Carlos Rivera: We have a quarterly patch cycle for non-critical issues and immediate patching for critical CVEs; there's a documented SLA for security updates in our security playbook. We'll share the patching policy.
[16:15] Maya Chen: I'll note to attach the security playbook and vulnerability management doc.
[16:40] Anita Patel: For evidence items in CAIQ—some rows ask for screenshots, others need policy text. Can you attach a sample audit log export and a screenshot of RBAC settings?
[16:55] Carlos Rivera: Yes, we'll provide a sanitized audit export, a screenshot of the RBAC roles UI, and a sample SCIM provisioning trace. Those will be in the CAIQ evidence bundle.
[17:30] Oliver Grant: On SLAs—are audit log delivery guarantees in SLA or are they best-effort?
[17:40] Maya Chen: For Dedicated we can include delivery guarantees as part of the SLA. For Hosted, log availability is covered under our enterprise package. We'll surface the exact SLA verbiage in the contract attachment.
[18:10] Samir Bose: Procurement will need to see indemnity and data breach notification timelines—what are your standard terms?
[18:22] Maya Chen: Our standard is 72-hour initial notification and cooperation; indemnity terms can be negotiated for enterprise engagements. We'll provide the standard legal addenda.
[18:40] Anita Patel: Do you have SOC 3 or public summaries we can include?
[18:48] Maya Chen: We have a SOC 2 Type II report for customers under NDA and a public security overview (SOC3 summary alternative) that we can link to.
[19:15] Oliver Grant: On model fallback/resilience—if a model endpoint is throttled, do you have automatic fallback to quantized variants to preserve latency? This is important for user-facing features.
[19:30] Carlos Rivera: Yes—our routing supports fallback tiers and quantized variants; we can configure SLO-based routing and automatic degrade-to-compact-model behavior.
[20:00] Anita Patel: For logging, does Redwood log prompt content or redact it in audit logs?
[20:12] Carlos Rivera: By default, prompt content is not stored long-term; audit logs record metadata and a hashed request id. For customers who enable full request logging, we recommend using Private deployment and configuring retention plus encryption.
[20:40] Maya Chen: We'll make sure to annotate the CAIQ where we marked data retention options.
[21:10] Samir Bose: There's a CAIQ row on third-party subprocessors—can you list your major subprocessors and any EU-specific ones?
[21:22] Carlos Rivera: Yes; we'll provide a subprocessors list. Major ones include our cloud provider compute/storage and a logging provider; we'll add a column in the CAIQ export for each subprocessor with location and contract status.
[22:00] Oliver Grant: For evidence, can you provide contact for your security team in case we need to validate items?
[22:10] Maya Chen: Sure—I'll include a security contact email and an SSO contact. For deep technical questions Carlos is the SE owner.
[22:35] Anita Patel: One more: do you support customer-managed encryption keys for model artifacts saved in dedup store?
[22:48] Carlos Rivera: Yes for Dedicated/Private we can support CMEK for artifact stores. For Hosted it's available via enterprise CMEK integrations with providers.
[23:20] Maya Chen: Let's go through a few CAIQ rows live so we can mark where attachments are required.
[23:38] (live CAIQ review, rapid back-and-forth)
[25:00] Maya Chen: I'm marking items: evidence A (SOC2 PDF), evidence B (RBAC screenshot), evidence C (audit export), evidence D (KMS/HSM attestation).
[25:30] Anita Patel: On the KMS/HSM attestation, we'll need vendor name and FIPS level.
[25:45] Carlos Rivera: We'll provide the cloud provider H S M attestation and indicate whether FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or higher is in use depending on customer's choice.
[26:18] Oliver Grant: For private peering and mutual TLS, is there a handshake spec we can test?
[26:30] Carlos Rivera: Yes, we'll provide an integration guide with mutual TLS cert exchange and expected cipher suites.
[27:00] Samir Bose: Procurement question: what's the expected lead time to spin up Dedicated region?
[27:12] Maya Chen: Typically 4-6 weeks for Dedicated capacity provisioning depending on capacity and region. We can accelerate in some cases.
[27:45] Anita Patel: Does Redwood support bring-your-own-GPU images on Private? We might want to run extra scanning of models.
[27:58] Carlos Rivera: Private supports customer-managed images in an air-gapped deploy but there are constraints. We'll capture the exact requirements and the image signing process.
[28:35] Oliver Grant: One CAIQ item asks about backup encryption keys rotation policy; can you give timeline?
[28:45] Carlos Rivera: Key rotation is configurable, recommended rotation every 90 days for keys protecting sensitive secrets; we document rotation policy in the KMS guide.
[29:20] Anita Patel: For logging retention beyond 90 days, what are costs and options?
[29:30] Maya Chen: We have a retention add-on priced by GB/day; we'll share the spreadsheet and options in the follow-up.
[30:05] Carlos Rivera: Also note that for EU residency we can set retention endpoints to EU S3 buckets and exclude cross-region replication.
[30:28] Oliver Grant: Great. On the CAIQ row about background checks for employees with access—what's your baseline?
[30:38] Carlos Rivera: We perform background checks for staff with production access and role-based vetting; we can provide HR policy samples as evidence.
[31:10] Anita Patel: Another item: Do you perform regular access recertification?
[31:20] Carlos Rivera: Yes, access recertification is part of our IAM process, typically quarterly for privileged roles.
[31:45] Maya Chen: We're approaching the last third of the call—any other items we should cover?
[31:55] Oliver Grant: We want to confirm how to handle legal/contractual evidence: will Redwood accept an NDA before sending some artifacts?
[32:05] Maya Chen: Yes we often deliver SOC2 under NDA; we'll default to that. I'll include a link to our standard NDA or we can sign Helix's template.
[32:40] Samir Bose: For final procurement gating, we need to see the SOC2, CAIQ filled, subprocessors list, KMS attestation, and a legal DPA.
[32:55] Maya Chen: Understood—we'll deliver that bundle.
[33:30] (brief pause as docs are pulled)
[34:05] Carlos Rivera: Quick technical note: model logs are separated from platform logs; you can opt into model-level request logging but that is treated as sensitive and has separate retention policies.
[34:24] Oliver Grant: If we enable model request logging, can we route logs to our SIEM and apply masking?
[34:35] Carlos Rivera: Yes you can route to SIEM, and we support masking at ingestion points; we recommend tokenization or redaction.
[35:10] Anita Patel: About breach response—can you walk through the 72-hour notification? What information can we expect?
[35:22] Maya Chen: Initial notification within 72 hours includes scope, impacted systems, and mitigation steps; follow-up reports with root cause and remediation timelines are delivered as available.
[35:50] Oliver Grant: On the SIG row about change management, what's your change approval board process?
[36:00] Carlos Rivera: We have a change advisory board for production changes; emergency changes follow an incident process with retrospective reviews. We'll provide the change management policy.
[36:30] Samir Bose: Anything else on legal side?
[36:40] Maya Chen: We'll include standard contract addenda; if Helix has specific requirements we can escalate to legal.
[37:05] Anita Patel: Ok let's recap next steps.
[37:15] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) Redwood to share SOC2 Type II report under NDA + CAIQ crosswalk and evidence bundle (SOC2 PDF, RBAC screenshot, audit export, KMS attestation) by 2025-08-23. 2) Carlos to prepare KMS/HSM technical notes and mutual-TLS guide by 2025-08-26. 3) Helix to return completed SIG baseline answers and confirm EU zones by 2025-08-28. 4) Schedule technical deep dive for HSM week of 2025-08-26.
[38:00] Anita Patel: That works. We'll share the NDA template if you prefer ours.
[38:12] Maya Chen: Fine—either is fine. We'll take your NDA if it's faster.
[38:40] (brief cross talk as links are pasted in chat)
[39:05] Samir Bose: Procurement will expect an itemized pilot pricing for Dedicated. Can you attach a sample?
[39:15] Maya Chen: We'll send pilot pricing and estimated lead times with the bundle.
[39:45] Oliver Grant: On the CAIQ evidence, please flag any items that will need additional engineering time from Helix.
[39:55] Carlos Rivera: We'll mark items as "Redwood artifact" vs "Customer action" in the CAIQ export.
[40:20] Anita Patel: Great. A couple minor clarifications: public cloud subprocessors list needs EU locations called out and contact for data processing agreement.
[40:32] Maya Chen: We'll include that in the subprocessor table.
[41:00] Carlos Rivera: One more technical note—our runtime supports client-side encryption for payloads if Helix wants end-to-end encryption before sending requests; we can support SDK examples.
[41:18] Oliver Grant: That could be useful. Please include SDK example and any performance notes.
[41:42] Maya Chen: Will do.
[42:05] (short silence as people gather thoughts)
[42:40] Anita Patel: Anything outstanding?
[42:50] Oliver Grant: Not from my side.
[43:05] Samir Bose: No.
[43:15] Maya Chen: Ok final recap in chat and I'll follow up with the bundle. Thanks everyone for the detailed review.
[43:30] Anita Patel: Thanks Maya and Carlos.
[43:38] (meeting ends at ~43:45 in transcript, actual recorded duration 47 minutes including recording overhead)
